#3353. IM8 Is David Beckham’s Answer to Late Nights, Long Flights, and Early Call Times

Nobody keeps a schedule like a touring artist. Red-eyes, soundchecks, 2 a.m. sets, and a call time the next morning that doesn’t care how late the show ran. Fans see the stage, but the real work is keeping your body ready to do it all again tomorrow.

David Beckham has lived his own version of that life for 30 years, from the soccer pitch, to fashion weeks, global campaigns, and co-owning Inter Miami CF.

“I’ve often felt overwhelmed by how many different products it takes to truly support your body,” the sporting icon says. So he co-founded IM8 with health sciences company Prenetics, and the brand’s most complete product now carries his name: the Beckham Stack.

The Beckham Stack pairs two products. Daily Ultimate Essentials Pro packs 90+ ingredients across 16 supplement categories, and Daily Ultimate Longevity adds 10 compounds for long-term cellular health, including 600 mg of NMN.

Together, they cover what a demanding schedule wears down. I give away a lot of keyboards. Sounds weird, I know, but stay with me here. I've reviewed dozens of keyboards. I once had a personal collection of around 40 boards on my wall. I've tested and used probably over a hundred boards, and probably edited the reviews of a hundred. In short, Tom's Guide senior writer Nikita and I test a lot of keyboards. And we have to give them away when we're done.

One of the main questions I ask people is, "do you want a mechanical keyboard or magnetic keyboard?" And the main response I get is, "what's the difference?"

In simple terms, it comes down to whether you're mostly gaming or typing. But like most things in life, the reality is a little more nuanced than that. Here's what you need to know, with a few of my top suggestions sprinkled in along the way.

The Keychron K2 HE is a magnetic keyboard, with tons of gaming features. But it's gasket mounted, making it extremely comfortable to type on for long periods of time. I should know, as I reviewed it, and I still use it for work on a regular basis as part of my keyboard rotation.

The non-halo version of my beloved NuPhy Halo75 V2, the Node75 ticks many of the same boxes. Beautiful styling, beautiful switches, beautiful keycap profile. I awarded the Node75 a full five stars in my review. It really is that good, especially for the money. And now it's even cheaper.

The main differences come down to whether you need certain gaming features, or whether you want a certain typing feel. However, there are some extra considerations to make... like sound.

The most compelling reason to buy a magnetic keyboard is for the gaming features. Magnetic switches actuate via magnetic resistance rather than a physical mechanism, so aren't tied down to a single fixed actuation point (i.e. a key depression point where the input is triggered). This opens up a plethora of awesome gaming features that you won't find even on a high-end mechanical gaming keyboard.

There's adjustable actuation, so you can set your keys to actuate with as little as 0.1mm of input. Multiple actuations per keystroke are also possible: you can set the W key so that halfway down is walk, and fully down is actually bound to Shift+W, so run.

And many keyboard manufacturers like Keychron and NuPhy have introduced other cool features that take advantage of magnetic detection, like NuPhy's 'Mod Tap', which changes the input based on how hard/fast you press the key.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

"What about Rapid Trigger?" I hear you call. "And Snap Tap?". I'm gettin' there! 'Rapid Trigger' allows repeat actuations without needing to recycle the switch fully to its reset point — you can basically spam faster. That's not physically possible on a mechanical switch, despite some manufacturers claiming their mechanical keyboards do it.

Last Key Prioritization, A.K.A. 'Snap Tap' is possible on a mechanical keyboard. This is a type of SOCD (simultaneous opposing cardinal direction) resolution. In other words: what the keyboard does when two opposites are inputted at the same time. 'Snap Tap' is just one of a few resolutions to this, and tells the board to prioritize the last key pressed, facilitating quick and easy counter strafing in games with interia-based accuracy penalties like "Valorant" and "Counter-Strike 2" (where it'll get you kicked). You can do this via firmware on a mechanical keyboard.

That doesn't mean mechanical switches are bad for gaming. Unless you're actually going to use any of the above features, ultra-snappy mechanical switches are perfectly fine for most casual and even some competitive gaming. They just don't offer you all the fancy bells and whistles of their magnetic counterparts.

Now, I've been rather pro-magnetic so far, haven't I. This is where the tables are turned. When it comes to typing experience, at least for now, traditional mechanical switches really have a leg up over magnetic. And it all comes down to how switches feel under your finger.

Mechanical switches offer a much more tactile experience, giving you feedback under your fingers. And I'm not just talking about 'Tactile' switches that have a mechanical bump. Even linear mechanical switches (with no mechanical bump) can give you a feeling different to magnetic switches, because they're typically designed with feel in mind — different weightings, springs and such will all affect how a linear switch feels.

In short, this makes typing more enjoyable. That said, there are some upsides to magnetic switches for typing. Adjustable actuation is the main benefit. You can dial in actuation points to wherever is best for you, which allows you to be as fast and accurate as possible. For example, I make far fewer mistakes at 2.6mm actuation, which in turn increases my type speeds as much as 5-10 words per minute. So I set all magnetic keyboards to 2.6mm when type testing (and usually have a work profile using 2.6mm).

There's a spanner in the works these days, too. Manufacturers are now launching true hybrid keyboards that can hot swap between both mechanical and magnetic switches. While Keychron and Gateron have recently launched the first (that I know of) tactile magnetic switch, giving the bumpy feel of a traditional mechanical tactile switch but the gaming features of a magnetic one. Up to now, all magnetic switches have been linear and smooth in operation — it's always felt a bit soulless to a tactile mechanical fan.

For now, though, there's still a much wider array of mechanical switches on offer, with different weights, feels and characteristics. So for typists interested in how their keyboard feels, I'd still recommend mechanical.

You'll also want to consider some other criteria. Mechanical keyboards designed with typing rather than gaming in mind tend to be more comfortable. They often use gasket mounts (where the PCB, switches and keycaps are suspended on rubber gaskets) which give you a comfy, bouncy feeling under your fingers.

Some gaming keyboards, or hybrid boards, use gasket mounts. Typically, though, performance magnetic gaming keyboards will use firmer mounts (top, plate, or tray mounts), which move about less. If your actuation is triggered in 0.1mm increments, you don't want your switches wobbling about.

Similarly, looks aren't really part of this debate, as any keyboard can be styled well or otherwise. Typically, though, custom mechanical keyboards tend to be designed with styling as a prime consideration, and therefore look a little more fun (speaking very generally).

Then, of course, there's sound. With the wider array of switches available on the market, and the fact they're built for the custom enthusiast market, mechanical boards tend to sound better. But there are bland examples found in both genres.

Finally, there's poll rates. But this is a bit of a non-issue. 8K polling is found on both magnetic and mechanical keyboards, but it's mostly snake oil. 1,000Hz found on many mechanical boards is more than enough for low latency gaming and to minimize the chance of missed inputs.

My primary advice here is this: just consider what you actually need. Don't be suckered in by all the marketing talk and fancy features. And don't think price is an issue. You can pick up magnetic and mechanical keyboards for under $50.

Are you going to be doing lots of competitive gaming where you need cutting edge performance features? If so, get a magnetic keyboard.

Do you care about a beautiful experience under your fingers? If so, you can consider a mechanical keyboard with lovely switches, or the ability to hot-swap between them. If you don't care about purist type-feel and just want raw speed and accuracy, a magnetic keyboard might still be best for heavy typists.

And here's the curve ball. Do you want the best of both? Then invest in a dual MX/HE keyboard, but be prepared to spend big bucks.

The Keychron K2 HE is a magnetic keyboard, with tons of gaming features. But it's gasket mounted, making it extremely comfortable to type on for long periods of time. I should know, as I reviewed it, and I still use it for work on a regular basis as part of my keyboard rotation.

In terms of sheer performance and polish versus cost, the NuPhy Air60 HE is my top Hall Effect gaming keyboard. It's a lot cheaper than the venerated Wooting 60HE+, yet offers just as many features and the companion software, NuPhy.io is (almost) as slick as Wooting's. For the money, though, this would be my pick. If you don't like low-profile, you could also check out the NuPhy FIeld75 HE.

This keyboard is a bit of a shameless rip off of the Wooting 60HE+... even down to the strap accessory. I haven't tested this exact model, but I have tested its bigger sibling, the HE75 Mag, and for under $50, these magnetic boards rule. You won't get the software polish of the Wooting board the HE60 emulates, or indeed of NuPhy or Keychron, but this is a budget pick after all... you can't have everything at this price.

The non-halo version of my beloved NuPhy Halo75 V2, the Node75 ticks many of the same boxes. Beautiful styling, beautiful switches, beautiful keycap profile. I awarded the Node75 a full five stars in my review. It really is that good, especially for the money. And now it's even cheaper.

The Rainy 75 Pro is probably the best sounding keyboard we've tested. It was so good that, even though my colleague reviewed it, I had to get one for myself. It's an absolute dream to type on too, thanks to the Kailh Cocoa switches.

If you're after a competent all-rounder mechanical board for typing and gaming on a budget, the Keychron C1 Pro 8K is my suggestion. This board is crazy cheap given its performance, switches and styling. The perfect entry-level mechanical board, if you ask me.

Discount with coupon! Remember when I said hybrid MX/HE boards don't come cheap? Yeah, the Lofree Hyzen is about as cheap as they come right now. Your other option is the slightly cheaper Keychron V6 Ultra Hybrid 8K HE, which is a better board and comes with a tactile magnetic switch, but it's still in pre-order until December.

#3349. 'The Challenge' Star Tyler Duckworth Cause of Death Revealed

"The Challenge" star Tyler Duckworth died from a heart issue ... TMZ has learned.

According to the North Dakota State Forensic Examiner’s Office, Tyler died from hypertensive cardiovascular disease ... and his manner of death was ruled natural.

Hypertensive cardiovascular disease is a heart condition caused by elevated blood pressure over years or decades.

As you know, Tyler died in August after being found in an overflowing bathtub. A downstairs neighbor complained of water coming through the ceiling ... and  "tried to get the water shut off" and was "not able to confirm" whether Tyler was alive.

We were told there were no outside signs of trauma found on Tyler's body.

He was honored that same month at his funeral, attended by his co-stars from both "The Real World" and "The Challenge."

Tyler made his final public appearance at a "Challenge Mania" event in Minneapolis just weeks before he died. He appeared on "The Challenge" in 2006, and won "Cutthroat" in 2010 and “Rivals” in 2011 before returning for "All Stars 2" in 2021.

#3348. Things 3.25 update brings new touch features to the MacBook Pro

Cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro. Version 3.25 builds on the task manager’s basic touch support so you can schedule a to-do with a swipe or select several tasks with two fingers and drag them all at once.

Say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow. Swipe right on the to-do to open the date picker. Open it by touch and you’ll see taller rows that make dates easier to tap. Custom menus get the same treatment.

Swiping left selects a to-do. Swipe left again to deselect it. For a longer list, swipe up or down with two fingers to select several items at once. Then touch and hold any selected item to pick up the whole group, even if some of those tasks are offscreen. You can also drag individual to-dos and headings.

A single tap selects a to-do, and a second tap expands it. Double-tapping works too. Inside a to-do, checklist items are easier to reorder by touch. You can also cancel a to-do or checklist item by pressing and holding its checkbox.

Cultured Code has also made the sidebar easier to resize with a finger and given buttons throughout the Mac app larger tap targets.

The update follows Siri AI and Spotlight integration in Things 3.24 and more flexible scheduling for repeating to-dos in Things 3.23. You can find Things for Mac on the Mac App Store.

#3347. You Can Get One of These Pocket E-Readers for As Little As $55 During Black Friday

Black Friday is usually a great time to grab a new e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a big discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is currently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink quickly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

The X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

These upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 launched at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also important to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing new firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

#3341. CarPlay Ultra coming to these cars, according to Apple

Last year, Apple officially announced CarPlay Ultra, the next-generation version of CarPlay that it first teased way back at WWDC 2022.

CarPlay Ultra first launched for Aston Martin owners in the United States and Canada. What about other automakers? Here’s what we know.

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

Updated November 24, 2026: Latest on Hyundai, more.

In December 2023, Apple said that Porsche and Aston Martin would be the first automakers to support next-generation CarPlay starting in 2024. That deadline came and went, and Apple confirmed in January that next-gen CarPlay had been delayed but was still in development.

Apple doesn’t offer a timeline on when CarPlay Ultra will actually be available through any other brand beyond Aston Martin. The company also does not have a dedicated list of automakers that have signed on to support CarPlay Ultra listed on its website.

When Apple announced the next-generation version of CarPlay at WWDC 2022, however, it stated that several brands had committed to supporting the platform. In May of last year, Apple touted that three new partners had signed on: Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis.

However, several brands have also dropped their plans to support CarPlay Ultra. Mercedes-Benz was originally on Apple’s list, but abandoned its plans to support next-generation CarPlay in 2024. According to the Financial Times, Audi, Volvo, Polestar, and Renault have also decided against supporting CarPlay Ultra, despite originally being touted as partners by Apple.

With all of that said, here is the full list of automakers who plan to eventually support CarPlay Ultra, as of November 2026.

What do we know beyond this list? Not a whole lot. Interestingly, Top Gear reported that the Hyundai IONIQ 3 EV would support CarPlay Ultra. Hyundai announced the IONIQ 3 in April, but has not commented on whether the vehicle will support CarPlay Ultra as rumors suggested.

Mark Gurman at Bloomberg has also reported CarPlay Ultra will launch for “least one major new Hyundai/Kia model in the second half of this year.”

While Apple has touted Ford as a partner for CarPlay Ultra, the automaker recently signaled it’s not too impressed with the first version of a platform.

In a recent interview, Ford CEO Jim Farley was asked whether the company is “considering” CarPlay Ultra support. Here’s what he said:

“We are. We don’t like the execution in round 1 of Ultra, but we’re very committed to Apple. I’ve talked to Tim many times about this.”

It’s better than a flat “no,” but perhaps not the enthusiasm Ford drivers might have hoped to hear.

The question at this point is whether any other automakers have ditched CarPlay Ultra. Ideally, Apple will provide a full list sooner rather than later, but in the meantime, this is the only information we have.

Black Friday isn't until November 27, but Amazon's early Black Friday 2026 sale is already bringing some decent discounts on TP-Link routers, with prices starting at $44.99 and savings of up to $100. The deals cover quite a few different networking needs, from compact travel routers that let you connect multiple devices to hotel wifi to more powerful home routers designed for faster internet plans and households with lots of connected devices.

TP-Link’s Roam routers are compact enough to travel with and let you share a hotel or public internet connection across your devices through a private Wi-Fi network—and right now, Amazon has three models on sale: the Roam 6 AX1500 for $44.99 (was $59.99), the Roam 6 AX3000 for $55.98 (was $79.99), and the Roam 7 BE3600 for $87.99 (was $119.99). All three support VPN connections and multiple operating modes, with the main differences coming down to speed. The AX1500 offers up to 1.5Gbps, the AX3000 doubles that and adds a 2.5Gbps WAN port, while the Wi-Fi 7-enabled Roam 7 reaches up to 3.6Gbps.

The TP-Link Archer AX21 V5 AX1800 is down to $54.99 from $89.99, saving you $35 on an affordable Wi-Fi 6 router for everyday home use. Its dual-band connection offers combined theoretical speeds of up to 1.8Gbps, which should be sufficient for typical activities like streaming, video calls, and browsing across several devices.

For homes with faster internet plans, multiple gamers, or lots of connected devices, TP-Link's Archer BE700 and BE770 offer tri-band Wi-Fi 7, including access to the 6GHz band for compatible devices. Both support EasyMesh for extended coverage and have 10Gbps WAN ports, although the BE770 provides faster wireless speeds and more wired connectivity. As for pricing, the TP-Link Archer BE700 is down to $248 from $349.99, saving you just over $100. It offers theoretical speeds of up to 15Gbps, a 2.5Gbps LAN port, and three Gigabit LAN ports. For just $52 more, the Archer BE770 (now $299.99, was $369.99) bumps speeds up to 18Gbps and adds a dedicated 10Gbps LAN port, making it better suited to high-speed network storage and large file transfers.

The TP-Link Deco BE25 is down to $99.98 from $129.99, saving you $30 on a Wi-Fi 7 router designed to work as part of a mesh network. It offers dual-band wireless speeds of up to 5Gbps, two 2.5Gbps Ethernet ports, and AI-driven roaming that helps connected devices switch between Deco units as you move around your home.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

#3331. Skip the knockoffs: Real PITAKA aramid fiber cases start at $18.99 this Black Friday

Scroll through Amazon for five minutes and you’ll find dozens of $10–20 cases that look, through a thumbnail, almost identical to $50+ aramid fiber ones. Same dark weave, same slim profile, same pitch.

Once you actually snap one onto a phone, the differences are obvious. You handle your phone for hours every day, so rough seams around the charging port, awkward cutouts, low-quality materials will make you regret your purchase instantly. With PITAKA’s Black Friday sale taking up to 30% off selected cases, it’s worth breaking down what actually separates a real aramid case from a cheap lookalike, why you should spent the extra money on PITAKA’s high-quality cases.

Plenty of budget cases get the woven look by printing a pattern onto plain plastic. If you’re looking for that style, go for it, but it won’t behave like woven aramid fiber, which lets a case stay rigid and thin without adding much weight.

Even genuine aramid cases aren’t all made the same way. The weave, resin, thickness, and surface finish all change how a case feels in use. PITAKA uses woven aramid fiber in two main weights: 600D and 1500D. Those numbers measure yarn density; the finer 600D weave feels a bit smoother and produces a slightly thinner shell than 1500D. Whatever case you choose, look past the word “premium” and check whether the maker actually spells out what the case is made of.

Most aramid cases stick to plain black and gray. PITAKA’s Fusion Weaving method blends colored fibers and multiple weave styles directly into the shell instead of printing a graphic on the outside. PITAKA says the process requires tight control over fabric tension and how fibers cross between layers. In practice, it means you can pick something colorful like the Sunset colorway without giving up the feel of woven fiber, or stick with classic Black & Grey if you prefer a quieter look.

Online listings spend almost all their time showing off the back of a case, even though your fingers spend just as much time on the sides, buttons, and bottom edge. An awkward camera cutout makes quick shots annoying, a tight port opening fights bulkier charging cables, and sharp edges dig into your hand on a long call.

Rather than selling one shell in ten colors, PITAKA splits its lineup into three builds:

If you use a magnetic charger, wallet, or grip, how the magnets are built into the case matters just as much as the outer material. Sticking a separate magnet ring inside a shell usually adds extra layers and thickness.

PITAKA’s Amber Magnet Film process bonds coated magnets directly with the aramid fiber and resin under heat and pressure. That keeps the magnets enclosed without bulking up the case, which is the kind of detail you won’t spot in a photo but will notice in your pocket.

Spending more on a case doesn’t guarantee it’s better, and plenty of $20 cases are completely fine. Genuine aramid fiber by itself doesn’t guarantee better drop protection either. A thin shell like Edge is made for people who hate bulky cases. If drop protection is your main concern, look at a cushioned option like Cairn or Summa, and compare actual edge coverage and model-specific testing instead of judging by price or material alone.

What you’re really paying for with a higher-end aramid case is how it feels and fits every time you pick up your phone.

If you already want a thinner, better-finished case, Black Friday takes some of the sting out of the price. PITAKA’s Amazon offers run November 19–30, with discounts varying by device and colorway:

Buying directly from the PITAKA official website? Code PTKPR12 takes an extra 5% off from November 10 through December 31. It’s separate from the Amazon sale, so double-check eligible products and your final total at checkout.

#3323. AirTag 2 has two big improvements that make it worth the upgrade

AirTag 2 (now only $18, down from $29) launched earlier this year after a five-year wait, and in my experience there are two big improvements that make it worth the upgrade.

Precision Finding is Apple’s best AirTag feature, letting you get step-by-step, highly precise directions to your lost item. But with the original AirTag, you had to be in fairly close proximity before you could benefit from Precision Finding.

With AirTag 2, Apple added a second-generation Ultra Wideband chip that makes Precision Finding now available from up to 1.5x farther away than before. It’s a huge increase that I’ve definitely noticed.

This expansion of Precision Finding to greater distances means the feature is now available a lot more often than with the old AirTag. For this reason alone, I highly recommend AirTag 2.

When you’re trying to find a lost item, Precision Finding isn’t the only tool AirTag offers. There’s also a built-in speaker that can play a sound, triggered by your iPhone, to help you track it down.

With AirTag 2, Apple has made the built-in speaker 50% louder than before. The company says this enables hearing it from up to twice as far away.

I’ve been impressed by how loud the AirTag speaker is able to get now. Between the new speaker and upgraded Precision Finding, Apple has made AirTag 2 better in the ways that users are likely to care about most.

You can buy AirTag 2 for $18 on Amazon (regularly $29) for a limited time.

Have you upgraded to AirTag 2? What’s your experience been like? Let us know in the comments.

Use Claude on Mac or Windows? Anthropic just released a new way to make personalized desktop apps using AI tools.

“Starting today, you can use Claude artifacts to create, run, and share desktop apps. The “Install as app” feature is rolling out in beta in Claude for Mac and Windows,” Anthropic says.

“When an artifact is installed as a Mac or Windows app, it gets its own icon and opens in its own window instead of inside Claude. You can share it with others, and it needs your permission before it can interact with your computer. You choose how much to allow.”

This form of Claude-created app is capable of sending notifications, adding items to the menu bar, and having its own permissions.

#3313. This iPad Is a Lifehacker 'Gift of the Year' Award Winner, and It's $50 Off During Black Friday

If you're shopping for an iPad this holiday season, you might be a bit intimidated by Apple's price tags. The iPad mini starts at $599; the base iPad Air is $749; and the entry-level iPad Pro is a whopping $1,199. Most of Apple's iPad line certainly lives up to its expensive reputation.

That's where the iPad A16 comes in. This is Apple's least expensive tablet, with an MSRP of $449. But despite being Apple's "budget" option, the iPad A16 shouldn't be ignored by customers looking for the best all-around device. In fact, it's really the best iPad for most people, which is why I named it the best tablet gift of 2026. What's more, retailers are giving the iPad A16 a $50 discount ahead of Black Friday, bringing the entry-level price down to $399.

The iPad A16 isn't Apple's best iPad (that would be the iPad Pro). It doesn't have the best display, the best camera, or the best processor. But it doesn't need those things: This iPad has a display, camera, and processor that are good enough for most use cases, without unnecessarily driving up the price. Simply put, it's one of the best tablets you can buy right now.

The iPad A16 has a large, 11-inch (technically 10.86 inches, according to Apple's fine print) IPS display with a brightness of 500 nits. As the name implies, it has Apple's A16 chip, the same processor as the iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 15. That chip is about four years old at this point, and while that means it won't be as fast as Apple's newer SoCs, it still holds its own with iOS 27. It comes with two cameras: One 12MP wide camera on the back, with support for 4K video recording, and a 12MP Center Stage camera on the front.

Apple says this iPad can run for 10 hours while browsing the internet on wifi or watching video. You charge the tablet with USB-C, which supports data transfer up to USB 2.0 (which nets you 480Mb/s transfer speeds). It also comes with other perks you might expect from Apple's more "pro" tablets. You can connect the iPad to an external display, up to 4K resolution at 60Hz. It also supports two Apple Pencil models: The USB-C Apple Pencil and the first-gen Apple Pencil.

The only real consideration here is storage: This model comes with 128GB of storage, which can run out fast. It's particularly usable for users who rely on cloud storage or mostly stream their entertainment. But if your giftee plans to store photos, videos, or music on their iPad, it's worth considering upgrading. The $50 discount applies to most storage models, as well as the cellular iPad options, except for the 512GB models: The wifi-only model has a smaller discount, while the cellular option has a $100 discount.

Sure, the iPad A16 doesn't have the fastest processor, an OLED display, support for newer accessories, or Apple's sharpest cameras. But all of the specs it does have are enough to run the things you need on iPadOS. If someone on your list is looking for an iPad for web browsing, streaming, messaging, and light gaming—and they don't need something for professional work—this device is likely more than enough iPad for them.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Yes, Apple participates in Cyber Monday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy, Amazon, and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

#3312. New Gemini setting lets you keep chat history, but turn off AI training [U]

Update 11/24: This new setting is now widely rolling out. On gemini.google.com, tap the settings gear icon to find a new “Gemini History” item at the very bottom. This opens myactivity.google.com/product/gemini with an On/Off dropdown.

Under “Help train generative AI models with,” you’ll find the new “Chat content including text & attachments” setting. It’s enabled by default.

Your future chats won’t be used to train generative AI models, unless you provide feedback.

Training on “Audio and Gemini Live videos & screenshares” remains an opt-in preference.

Original 11/16: Gemini’s existing Keep Activity setting “controls how long your chats are saved and whether they are used to train generative AI models.”

Google is now separating that preference into two new options.

This is huge. One of the major things Siri-AI users on iPhone like to point out is that while their assistant is a less capable portmanteau of Siri and Gemini, their queries are not used for AI training. Gemini on Android, on the other hand, offers the superior AI platform with the caveat that there is no way to opt out of training and still retain your chat history. Until now. Now users of Gemini on Android get the best of both worlds - the best of Google's AI models powering their AI experiences and their chat history siloed from AI training.

The first setting is called “History” and lets you “control how long your history is saved.” If disabled:

“…future chats will be saved for around 2 months and used to respond to you, process your feedback, and protect Google, its users, and the public, with help from human reviewers.”

The duration is currently 24 hours for chat context, and 72 hours to help protect Google, users, and the public.

The second setting allows you to “separately control whether your chat content, including text and attachments, is used to train generative AI models.”

With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training.

If Keep Activity is currently off, the two “new settings will both be off.” These changes are rolling out over the “coming weeks,” and Google is notifying users via email.

#3309. Doha Winners: ‘A Girl Unknown’ & ‘Concrete Land’ Scoop Top Prizes

Chinese director Zou Jing’s A Girl Unknown won the top $75,000 Best Narrative prize at the Doha Film Festival as the second edition of its revamped format came to a close on Friday evening.

The China-set first feature follows the fate of a young girl who is found abandoned as a baby in a rubbish bin and then grows up from babyhood through to adolescence with three sets of different guardians and circumstances.

The film world premiered in Cannes Critics’ Week earlier this year where it won the Fipresci Prize. The picture was acquired for the U.S. by Greenwich Entertainment which is planning an early 2027 tour and release. Related Stories News International Insider: Doha Days; Tricky Week For BAFTA; 'Remarried Empress' Interview News Todd Boehly Dissects How Daniel Katz's Trading Desk Acumen Fed Into A24 Success: "Very Few Entertainment People Understand Math"

Rafael Manuel won Best Artistic Achievement in Narrative for Filipiñana about a 17-year-old girl who discovers a rotten side to the posh countryclub where she works on the golf course. The film world premiered in Sundance, where it won the World Cinema Special Jury Award. The film is the Philippines’ entry for the 99th Academy Awards. Watch on Deadline

Best Actress was awarded posthumously to Josette Kwanya for her performance in her son Auguste Bernard Kouemo’s House of the Wind as an elderly Cameroonian woman waiting for her children to return home after they left for Europe in search of fresh life opportunities.

The film won Venice’s Lion of the Future for a Debut Film when it premiered there in its Orizzonti sidebar in September.

This year’s jury was presided over by Japanese director Naomi Kawase, who was joined by by Oscar-winning documentarian Gianfranco Rosi, rising actor Adam Bessa, Tunisian producer Dora Bouchoucha and Palestinian director Kamal Aljafari.

In further prizes, Best Documentary went to Asmahan Bkerat’s Concrete Land about a Bedouin family struggling to preserve their traditional way of life in tents, as well as the Fipresci prize, which is being awarded at the festival for the first time this year.

In other documentary prizes, Tala Hadid’s Bardi won the Best Artistic Achievement for Documentary.

Fatma Hassan Alremaihi, Festival Director and CEO of Doha Film Institute said the 2026 Doha Film Festival tapped into her institute’s belief in “the power of stories to transcend borders, challenge perspectives and bring the experiences of people and communities into the global conversation.”

“At Doha Film Institute, we believe that important voices deserve to be seen, heard and recognised. Doha Film Festival exists to provide that platform, bringing together filmmakers and audiences from across the world, championing bold and independent storytelling, and creating space for stories that might otherwise go untold,” she said.

“The films we honour tonight remind us that cinema is not simply a reflection of the world we live in; it is a force that can shape how we understand it, connect with one another and imagine a more empathetic future.”

#3308. Apple Mail added four convenient new features in iOS 27

iOS 27 brought new features to Apple Wallet, Maps, Notes, Messages, and more—and it includes key upgrades for the Mail app too. Here’s everything new for Apple Mail in iOS 27.

If you have much history using Apple Mail, you’ll know that its search feature hasn’t always been the best. But in iOS 27, search has gotten a big upgrade.

More relevant search in Mail. A new ranking system brings the most relevant results to the top to help you find what you need right away — even if it’s buried deep in your inbox.

I can’t count the number of times search has previously failed to find messages that I knew existed. So far in my usage, iOS 27 has fixed that.

Suggestions at the top of messages have been in Apple Mail for years. But in iOS 27, they have a new, more flexible design and expand to support third-party apps.

When Mail detects that you might want to take action on the contents of an email, a suggestion might appear at the top of the message. These include: directions in Maps, creating events in Calendar, tracking a shipment with Apple Wallet, and more.

In iOS 27, third-party apps can offer suggestions too. And when multiple apps are available with suggested actions, there’s a drop-down menu to show you all available options.

Smart Reply is a keyboard feature that automatically surfaces reply options you can utilize with a single tap.

In iOS 27, the next generation of Apple Intelligence comes with improvements to Smart Reply.

Apple says that Smart Reply “can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.” Essentially, rather than offering fairly generic reply options, now Smart Reply suggestions will actually sound a lot more like you.

Apple has added ‘Ask Siri’ buttons throughout Apple Mail, just like the rest of its system apps. And Siri AI brings a bunch of new powers for Mail users.

One example I’ve seen several times on social media is that you can ask Siri to delete all messages from a specific sender that’s spamming you.

I asked the new Siri on iOS 27 to delete Spam emails from a particular adddess and it just did that so seamlessly pic.twitter.com/EYn74buYAX

Beyond new features, Apple also says that iOS 27 makes the Mail app run better than ever thanks to bug fixes and performance improvements. Here are some specific examples given:

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Black Friday is upon us, and there's no shortage of discounted smartphone deals available for you to take advantage of right now. However, one Black Friday phone deal you should probably avoid is the iPhone 16e. For some reason the ageing e-series iPhone is trending, despite the fact that the iPhone 17e is available — and much better value for money.

I was a little confused about why people would be hunting for iPhone 16e deals, seeing as how it's coming up to its second birthday. So I went looking to see if there were any deals that might have knocked the phone down to an enticing price. Sadly I had very little success.

There's always been demand for older iPhones, and I've come across people trying to convince me that the positively ancient iPhone 5c is gaining traction with the youth of today. I don't buy that, but I'll admit that I haven't looked into it. Anyway...

The fact that flagship iPhones are so expensive and hold their value compared to similarly-priced Androids means that people gravitate towards older models due to the lower price tag. Phones like the iPhone 16e, which started life as a relatively cheap option have the capacity to drop even further, which bolsters their long-term popularity.

Which I totally understand. The downside is that unused iPhones don't stick around for more than a couple of years, and the iPhone 16e is in that situation right now. When I went hunting for deals, the majority of listings I found were for used or refurbished handsets. I don't have anything against used phones, but they're not the kind of thing a lot of people would expect when Black Friday rolls around.

The only brand new deal I could find was at Walmart, with an iPhone 16e that's locked to Walmart's Straight Talk carrier — an MVNO powered by Verizon. While the phone is $200, I'm not sure that it's the right deal for most people.

Grab the iPhone 16e at Walmart for just $199. The only caveat is that this phone is locked to the retailer's Straight Talk MVNO. Still you get a nice display, A18 performance, a solid solo camera and access to Apple Intelligence.

For starters, picking up a Walmart iPhone 16e means you are locked into Straight Talk for at least a year. The carrier's unlock policy mimics that of Verizon, and it means you have to have owned your phone for at least 365 days before it can be unlocked.

By which point the iPhone 18e will have been released, and the iPhone 19e likely only be months away. This means that the iPhone 16e will be borderline obsolete by next November.

On top of that, I actually found some deals for the iPhone 17e that are a lot cheaper. While the difference between the phones isn't enormous, the upgrades Apple afforded to the 17e make it a much more enticing handset — including MagSafe and improved performance from the A19 chipset. However, these deals do come with some caveats of their own.

Get your iPhone 17e for just $0.43 a month at AT&T, no trade-in required. All you need to do is sign up for an eligible 36-month plan and Apple's cheapest handset can be yours for less than $16.

As you can see, AT&T is offering the iPhone 17e for $0.43 a month over a 36 month contract. That means the total you'd pay for the phone itself is $15.48. That's pretty incredible for a phone that was released back in February.

Meanwhile a model with 512GB of storage is $6.43 a month, which works out to a total cost of $231.48. It's not the same kind of discount, but it's still a hefty price cut.

AT&TB isn't the only carrier with deals either, since T-Mobile is offering a free iPhone 17e.

Apple iPhone 17e: was $699 now free w/ T-Mix plan @ T-Mobile

Grab a free iPhone 17e at T-Mobile, so long as you sign up for a 36-month T-Mix plan and meet the other eligibility criteria. That includes signing up for a new line and porting your old number, or trading in an old device first.

The downside here is that you need to meet a bunch of T-Mobile's criteria. The first is to sign up to a T-Mix plan with at least one monthly "Pick" perk while porting your number from another carrier and opening a new line. Alternatively a new line and trade-in is an option, but you need to add an extra Pick to your plan — and pay the additional cost.

Still, free is free, and that's a lot less than $15.48. Though the caveat is both devices will be locked into that specific plan for another three years — at which point the iPhone 20e could be on the way.

While I'm well aware that the jump from iPhone 16e to iPhone 17e wasn't that big, I'm personally more inclined to pick the 17e. Not only because the deals cost less money upfront, but also because the addition of MagSafe is a huge benefit. I'm a big fan of MagSafe's accessory support, and that makes the 17e a much more useful phone.

That said, the iPhone 17e deals are locking you into three year plans, which may not be something you want to do. Especially when the alternative is being locked into Straight Talk for a year.

In the end, the right decision is the one that you make for yourself.

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

Nothing's first over-ear headphones, the Headphone (1), is $130 off for Black Friday, bringing them down to $169 from $299 (their lowest price ever). Nothing's newer Headphone (a), which launched in 2026 and earned an "excellent" rating in PCMag's review, is on sale as well, dropping to $109 from $199. For more discounts and the latest offers, check out our extensive Black Friday 2026 coverage.

In line with the company’s design language, these headphones feature transparent elements and bold, geometric detailing that make them stand out from typical matte-black pairs. But the appeal goes beyond the look. These IP52-rated headphones use 40mm drivers, hybrid ANC, and both USB-C and 3.5mm connectivity. They also support high-res audio via LDAC, while Nothing’s companion app gives you basic and advanced EQ controls for adjusting the sound. Battery life is impressive, too, stretching to 35 hours with ANC on and up to 80 hours with it switched off.

But the hardware alone doesn’t define the experience—Nothing’s control scheme is what makes these wireless headphones stand out. Instead of touch panels or clunky buttons, you get a satisfying volume scroll wheel (they call it the Roller), a multi-function Paddle for track navigation, and a customizable button that can switch EQ profiles or noise modes. You also get spatial audio and multipoint Bluetooth support, which work well across Android and iOS.

That said, the earcups aren’t the softest for long sessions, and while they’re padded, the shape might not suit everyone. Performance-wise, the ANC handles low-end noise well (think airplane engines and AC hum) but struggles with sharper, unexpected sounds like clanging dishes or chatter nearby. As for its sound profile, it leans towards the punchier side, especially with a bit of EQ tweaking in the app, but you’ll need to put in some effort if you want the best results, notes this PCMag review.

#3304. David Byrne On Getting Into Character As Elon Musk For ‘Musk’ Song “Let Me Sell You A Dream” – Crew Call Podcast

On today’s Crew Call we chat with near EGOT winner David Byrne about “Let Me Sell You A Dream,” his new song for Alex Gibney’s controversial documentary Musk about, yes, Elon Musk.

Byrne tells us about co-writing the ditty during the European leg of his latest tour “Who is the Sky?” and biking to a London musical equipment shop to get recording gear, so he could create a makeshift studio in his hotel room and lay down tracks for Oscar nominated composer Daniel Pemberton, who is a co-writer on the song.

In recording the tune, Byrne exclaims, “I’d sit at my little mic stand in a hotel room and I’d go into character as Elon Musk (exhale), and just start ranting.”

Off the bat, “Let Me Sell You a Dream” in its fast dance tempo brings to mind the 1986 Talking Heads single “Wild Wild Life” which Byrne wrote for the Warner Bros absurdist reality movie he directed and co-wrote, True Stories. Watch on Deadline

Byrne says that “Let Me Sell You a Dream” had to be “hard hitting…It’s going to have an impact at the at the end. It has to jump right in, and grab you by the throat.”

“It’s not one of those fading-while-the-credits roll and everybody decides, ‘I’m going to get up, get out and get back to my car before everybody else.'”

“Let Me Sell You a Dream” is also throwback to the types of pseudo anti-yuppie tunes that Talking Heads was known for including 1988’s “(Nothing) But Flowers” and 1979’s “Life During Wartime”. Byrne explains that the Musk end-credits song was arguably the “fastest” he has ever written in his career. To date, while Musk has railed against Gibney about the documentary, he hasn’t sent any praise or tomatoes to the Oscar winning Byrne. Give a listen to Byrne’s process here:

Byrne also takes us down memory regaling that his first instrument was a violin, and how he grew up inspired by The Rolling Stones and Motown. He also chats about the early days of the Talking Heads when they were discovered by Sire Records’ boss Seymour Stein (“He could meet with us, talk with us and and sing ours songs back to us”) as well as working with Bernardo Bertolucci and producer Jeremy Thomas on the score for The Last Emperor which won Byrne an original score Oscar which he co-shared with Cong Su and Ryūichi Sakamoto.

A time when Byrne was told by the music industry he was too audacious? How about when he did his first solo album in 1989, the Latino infused “Rei Momo”?

“They implied that I shot myself in the foot and that the fans were going to leave,” said Byrne, which if you look at the full houses for his concerts, not to mention the Broadway run of his concert show American Utopia is definitely not the case: His appearance last November at the Dolby Theater drew the likes of Oliver Stone, Judd Apatow and Derek Waters, while his Hollywood Bowl late August appearances for “Who Is The Sky?” were jam packed.

“I thought that if I keep trying different things, you’re not going to get pigeonholed as being the blues rock band or the funk band,” Byrne shares, “I thought if I can do different things, that’s going to give you wiggle room, and allow you to do different things down the road and hopefully the audience goes with you.”

And of course, we ask the never-ending question to Byrne, that even after a great reunion with the Talking Heads for the A24 Imax 2023 re-release of seminal concert film Stop Making Sense, will they ever tour together again?

#3303. The Apple Watch Series 11 Is $100 Off in Walmart's Black Friday Sale

If you’ve been counting down to Black Friday and hoping for a deal on an Apple Watch, there’s no time like the present: Walmart recently launched its early Black Friday tech deals, and the rarely discounted Apple Watch Series 11 is currently $100 off, bringing the 42mm GPS model down to $299 (originally $399). The 46mm GPS model is $329 (originally $429), while the GPS + Cellular versions start at $399 and are also $100 off.

Though it has been supplanted by the Series 12, released earlier this fall, the Series 11 is still a great buy. It lasts up to 24 hours, making it a great option for everyday use and sleep tracking, and a 15-minute charge provides around eight hours of use. It has a strong selection of health features, including wrist temperature sensing, sleep score, ECG, heart-rate monitoring, and hypertension notifications, as well as detailed workout tracking. Compared with the Series 10, this aluminum model’s Ion-X display is twice as scratch-resistant. It’s also water-resistant to 50 meters.

While it doesn’t have the Series 12’s new processor or updated health-tracking features, the Apple Watch Series 11 is a great pick for your first Apple Watch or as an upgrade from an older model, such as the Series 8. Its large display, durability, and versatile staple features deliver the core Apple Watch experience at a more affordable price, especially if you don’t want Apple’s latest Audio Intelligence features.

#3301. PrismML’s Bonsai 2.5 brings better coding and tool use to on-device AI

Back in July, PrismML claimed its roughly 4 GB, 1-bit Bonsai 27B was the first AI model of its size to run on an iPhone. Now PrismML has released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an update to the model it introduced in September.

The startup also drew attention when CEO Babak Hassibi told CNBC that Apple was evaluating its technology, as we reported at the time.

The new model is based on Qwen3.8 27B and keeps the same 5.9 GB footprint in its most compact format. This time, PrismML focused on helping the model handle longer tasks, including figuring out what to do when a tool returns an unexpected result or a step fails.

Bonsai 2.5 improved on six of the seven benchmarks PrismML highlights. Its SWE-bench Verified coding score rose from 60.8 to 75.6, while its AppWorld tool-use score jumped from 51.2 to 90.5. LiveCodeBench v6 dipped from 83.8 to 83.0.

What could that look like on a Mac? A coding assistant could inspect a private project, make a change, run the tests, and use the results to revise its fix. A document app could summarize a folder of sensitive files while keeping the processing on the device.

PrismML says Bonsai 2.5 runs on Mac, iPhone, and iPad through MLX. Its Apple silicon package is about 8.9 GB, and the model card walks through setup on a Mac. The weights are available for free under Apache 2.0.

For a closer look at how the model was compressed and tested, read PrismML’s technical white paper.

Thursday was a dual celebration for Justin Timberlake‘s visit with Jimmy Fallon on NBC’s Tonight Show: There was Thanksgiving, of course, which you can see in the photo above was most certainly not ignored by the two old friends, and then for the former boy bander the visit was an opportunity to celebrate the 20th anniversary of his album FutureSex/LoveSounds.

And of course there’s always new material to plug, and last night it was Timberlake‘s four-part doc series streaming on Apple TV beginning December 11.

The Thanksgiving visit began with Timberlake joining Fallon in a musical number celebrating “The History of Party Songs.” With Timberlake initially putting up some mock reluctance, the two then launched into Soul II Soul’s “Back to Life (However Do You Want Me),” then proceeded through a smorgasbord of classic dance hits, including Ini Kamoze’s “Here Comes the Hotstepper,” Mark Morrison’s “Return of the Mack,” Montell Jordan’s “This Is How We Do It,” Spice Girls “Wannabe,” Bell Biv DeVoe’s “Poison,” Timberlake’s own “Rock Your Body,” Wild Cherry’s “Play That Funky Music White Boy,” “Good Times” by Chic, Cool and the Gang’s “Celebration,” and some others you might be able catch before the big finish of The Backstreet Boys’ “I Want It That Way.” Related Stories News Ariana Grande Crashes Jimmy Fallon's Monologue With 'Focker-In-Law's Ben Stiller & Robert De Niro Late Night TV 'Tonight Show': Jimmy Fallon & Jamie Lee Curtis Channel Fielder & Holmes In Cold Open

Watch the musical medley here: Watch on Deadline

Timberlake also reflected on the making of the FutureSex/LoveSounds album, noting that at the time of its recording he’d been listening to “Bowie, David Byrne, Talking Heads, Freddie Mercury, Queen, Billy Idol, James Brown, Eurythmics, INXS…but we were kind of thinking, How we can take the sonics of dance music and flip it?”

Timberlake recalls that, as presented in the upcoming docuseries, his record label at the time was not initially impressed with the album, thinking it was “too fast,” to which Timberlake responded, “That’s why it’s going to work.” He also remembered that the label was disappointed that he wasn’t using his signature falsetto enough. “I was listening to [David Bowie’s] ‘Rebel Rebel’ a lot…and that music at that time sounded so daring.” Timberlake says he wanted to create the impression that the singer was a character in the song, as Bowie so often did, and the result was “SexyBack.”

Regarding the upcoming four-part Timberlake documentary series, the singer explained that he overcame his initial reluctance – “I’m sort of famously private” – by trusting director and friend Fisher Stevens. “I feel like I’ve gone through a lot in the last five years that made me a better human,” he said.

“But the more we sat down and talked, the more I found myself searching for something that was beneath the surface a little more,” he continued. “And I think that at the end of the day I sort of mustered up some courage to talk about things that I’ve never talked about before. Things that even those that are closest to me don’t know.”

Timberlake also paid tribute to the late singer-songwriter D’Angelo, the major influence who died October 14, 2025. “D’Angelo, for me, he changed everything,” Timberlake told Fallon. “You know, he was one of those artists. Rest in peace. What a brilliant, brilliant, brilliant artist. But I remember when he came out, it just like everything changed. [He] was a once-in-a-generation artist.”

And finally, here’s Timberlake’s performance that capped the Fallon appearance, taking place at New York’s famed Rainbow Room atop 30 Rock. He performs a medley of “FutureSex/LoveSound,” “SexyBack,” “Summer Love” and “My Love.”

The docuseries Timberlake airs on Apple TV on Friday, December 11 with the first two episodes, followed by the third episode on Friday, December 18 and the finale on Wednesday, December 23, 2026.

#3299. This Bose Portable Bluetooth Speaker Is 33% Off for Black Friday

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

A price drop always stands out more when the product in question already has a reputation for delivering above its size, and that’s the case with the Bose SoundLink Plus. It hasn’t been on the market for long, but it’s already earned strong reviews—CNET labeled it “the Goldilocks of Bose Bluetooth speakers.” And right now, for Black Friday, it’s down to $179, which is the lowest price we've seen.

Bose positions it right in the middle of the SoundLink lineup, and you feel that balance in how it’s built. It’s compact enough to clip onto a backpack using its built-in nylon strap, and tough enough to handle getting knocked around, and sealed against dust and full water submersion with an IP67 rating. Battery life can last up to 20 hours, depending on the volume, which is sufficient for full-day outings. On the connectivity side, there’s Bluetooth 5.4 with AAC and AptX Adaptive support, as well as the ability to keep two devices paired for smoother switching. What you don’t get is a microphone, an aux port, or any voice assistant support, which is worth considering if you prefer wired options or use speakers for calls.

As for its sound profile, it leans into mid- and high-bass, which gives electronic and pop tracks a lively pulse, though at higher volumes, you may notice some compression (which is common in speakers this size). It also doesn’t reach into true low-bass territory, so anyone who wants thumping sub-bass may not get it here, but the punch it does deliver feels clean for its size, notes this PCMag review. And while you won't get the width and separation of a stereo mix since the SoundLink Plus plays audio in mono, its directivity is good—meaning its sound remains clear from different listening positions, so you don't have to sit directly in front of it to get a good experience.

#3298. An annoying ‘mistake’ in macOS was actually prep for the latest MacBook Pro

You may remember that Apple made a seeming mistake in the user interface for macOS 26, meaning that attempts to resize windows would often fail. The reason for this has now become clear, and Apple has done something both fun and clever in macOS 27 to resolve it …

I was one of a number of people to note that trying to grab the corner of a window in macOS Tahoe in order to resize it would often fail. Developer Norbert Heger pointed out this is because Apple changed the radius of the corners without changing the grabbable area.

It turns out that my initial click in the window corner instinctively happens in an area where the window doesn’t respond to it. The window expects this click to happen in an area of 19 × 19 pixels, located near the window corner. If the window had no rounded corners at all, 62% of that area would lie inside the window. But due to the huge corner radius in Tahoe, most of it – about 75% – now lies outside the window.

At the time, the radius change itself looked like an inexplicable mistake on Apple’s part, and the company did revert it. However, Macworld’s Michael Simon appears to have discovered the reason for the original change.

The new rounder corners on the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR are basically a perfect match for the macOS 26 radii.

So if you move a window to the corner of the new machine, it would fit perfectly. However, since Apple reverted the corner radius, it would no longer do so. The company solved this by a clever UI transition.

What’s happening there is Golden Gate’s 20-point corner radius is subtly and gradually expanding when It approaches the bottom corner of the screen to match the exact corner of the display, which is much larger. I can’t be certain it’s exactly 26-point, but it sure looks like it to me. The effect is incredible. I’ve watched it like 20 times and I can barely see it changing, yet when it reaches the corner it’s perfectly expanded to match.

You can see this illustrated by a GIF in the Macworld piece. While the original change annoyed me, Apple’s solution is the perfect example of the company sweating the details.
